claim: The Last Supper canvas is viewable free of charge in the abbey church Mon-Sat 8-11am and 1-5pm, Sundays 8-10am and 1-5pm, with a push-button 5-minute timer light in the side aisle; abbey address is Abdijstraat 40, 2260 Tongerlo, Belgium.
quote: The painting is displayed in the abbey church: Weekdays (Mon-Sat): 8-11 am and 1-5 pm; Sundays: 8-10 am and 1-5 pm. The light can be switched on with a push button in the side aisle (5 min. timer). Free admission.

claim: Tongerlo Abbey was founded c.1130 by Norbertines from Sint-Michielsabdij in Antwerp on the estate of Giselbert van Castelré; the community was dissolved in 1796 during the French Revolution and re-established in 1838-1840.
quote: De Abdij van Tongerlo is een norbertijnenabdij bij het dorp Tongerlo in de Belgische gemeente Westerlo. De abdij werd gesticht rond 1130, toen een aantal norbertijnen van de Sint-Michielsabdij te Antwerpen zich vestigden op het landgoed van heer Giselbert van Castelré.

claim: The Tongerlo Last Supper canvas measures just over 8 x 4 meters and was painted 1507-1508 in Milan; recent multispectral and IRR analysis by Jean-Pierre Isbouts attributes details such as St. John's face directly to Leonardo, with Giampietrino, Andrea Solario and Marco d'Oggiono identified as collaborators.
quote: The canvas measures just over 8 x 4 meters, created between 1507-1508 in Milan as a replica of the famous mural. Giampietrino, Andrea Solario and Marco d'Oggiono were identified as the principal collaborators of da Vinci's Milanese studio.

claim: The Da Vinci Museum closed on 1 November 2021 for canvas restoration; since summer 2025 the Last Supper hangs again in the abbey church, while the Tiendschuur (tithe barn) shows a full-scale high-resolution photographic reproduction.
quote: The Da Vinci museum closed on November 1, 2021 for restoration and relocation of the Last Supper, with the restoration of the canvas completed in early 2025. Since summer 2025, Leonardo da Vinci's masterpiece shines again in full glory in Tongerlo on its new old location: in the abbey church.

claim: Public guided tours run every first Sunday of the month (April-October) at 2pm from the abbey gate for 6 euros (free for under-12s); group tours of 25 people cost 70 euros, last 90 minutes and cover the inner courtyard, tithe barn and abbey church, bookable via Toerisme Westerlo with three weeks' notice.
quote: Every first Sunday of the month at 2 PM, guides welcome visitors at the abbey gate for a guided walk on the inner courtyard. Tickets cost 6 euros. The cost for groups is 70 euros per 25 people. The guided tour lasts 90 minutes and covers the inner courtyard, tithe barn, and abbey church.

claim: Tongerlo abbey beer has been brewed by Brouwerij Haacht in Boortmeerbeek since 1990 and carries the Recognized Belgian Abbey Beer label since 1999; on-site brewing at the abbey ended in WWI when the occupier confiscated the copper kettles.
quote: Tongerlo is a Belgian abbey beer that is brewed at Brouwerij Haacht in Boortmeerbeek in accordance with the Abbey of Tongerlo. This beer has carried the label of Recognized Belgian Abbey Beer since 1999. The brewing in the abbey came to a final end when during World War I, the occupier confiscated the copper brewing kettles.

claim: On-site amenities at the abbey include a bookshop called De Oude Linden in a converted carriage house, plus a bakery; the abbey church dates to 1852 and the complex spans buildings from the 15th to 18th centuries.
quote: The abbey features a bakery and hostel bakery. A bookshop called De Oude Linden operates in a converted carriage house. The abbey includes a church (built 1852), meeting house for group retreats, and multiple historic buildings spanning from the 15th to 18th centuries.

claim: Torenhof Brasserie sits directly opposite the Tongerlo Abbey gate, serving Flemish and Belgian seasonal dishes with a children's menu, and operates an adjacent bakery and ice-cream café in the park garden.
quote: Torenhof Brasserie. Situated in Westerlo, tegenover de Abdij van Tongerlo (opposite Tongerlo Abbey). The establishment features an extensive menu offering Vlaamse en Belgische gerechten (Flemish and Belgian dishes) with seasonal ingredients and regional products.

claim: Abbot Arnoud Streyters purchased the Last Supper canvas in 1545 for 450 Rhenish florins; it is considered the most faithful replica of Leonardo's original because the Milan fresco has heavily deteriorated.
quote: The abbey has housed the most faithful and most beautiful replica of the Last Supper, which Leonardo da Vinci painted since 1545. This copy is valuable because the original fresco in Milan's Santa Maria delle Grazie has deteriorated significantly over time.
